purpose: Version-specific modeling guidance; not approval or PT acceptance.
method: Direct visual inspection of the actual native photograph and matching massa/ohje images. No silhouette masks or IoU artifacts consulted.

findings.observation: Behind the left part of the far wing, immediately left/back of its central domed pavilion, the photograph renders an open rectangular inner court with visible inward-facing walls. The corresponding source area reads as a continuous raised sloping/curved roof mass.
findings.modelingGuidance: Retain the source roof mass at this location rather than opening the generated rectangular well.

findings.observation: The far wing facade extends slightly farther downward toward the right frame edge than the source contour, making that side of the courtyard a little more compressed.
findings.modelingGuidance: Keep the native source facade footline and diagonal projection.

cameraAndMassObservation: The distinctive diagonal composition is preserved: the close roof band enters from the bottom-left and crosses the bottom edge, while the far wing enters at the clipped top-left and descends toward the right edge. The near pavilion and foreground crops closely follow the source; the photograph has not been converted into a symmetric frontal view.
geographyObservation: The open courtyard remains between the two diagonal palace bands. A street, trees and city buildings sit behind the far wing along the upper edge. No river is inserted into the courtyard, and no river is visible in this tight composition.
literalHavainnekuva: Present, readable and correctly spelled at top-left.
photographicSurfaceQuality: Credible limestone, slate/lead roofs, paving, roof ornament and coherent strong daylight. The broad dark glazed roof area on the far-right block reads as roofing rather than a free-standing pyramid.
